scenario_text: A government-owned insurance company needs a claims processing portal for rural customers. All requirements have already been documented in a 200-page RFP. The portal must comply with IRDAI regulations. The team has 15 developers, funding is approved for 18 months, and the requirements will not change once signed off.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a user-friendly interface for rural customers to submit claims
requirements.business_justification: Rural customers have limited technical expertise; simple interface increases adoption rates
requirements.assumptions: Users have basic computer knowledge and access to the internet
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Portal's claim submission form has a maximum of 5 steps and uses clear, concise language

requirements.statement: The system shall integrate with existing insurance company databases for claims processing
requirements.business_justification: Integration reduces manual data entry errors and increases processing speed
requirements.assumptions: Existing databases are accessible via APIs or web services
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Claims data is successfully retrieved and processed within 2 hours of submission

requirements.statement: The system shall store and manage claims data in compliance with IRDAI regulations
requirements.business_justification: Compliance with regulations ensures data security and integrity
requirements.assumptions: IRDAI regulations are up-to-date and accurately reflected in the system
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System logs and audit trails are maintained for 5 years and are accessible for regulatory review

requirements.statement: The system shall provide real-time updates to customers on claim status
requirements.business_justification: Real-time updates increase customer satisfaction and reduce inquiries
requirements.assumptions: Customers have access to the internet and can receive email notifications
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Customers receive email notifications within 30 minutes of claim status update

requirements.statement: The system shall be scalable to handle increased traffic during peak periods
requirements.business_justification: Scalability ensures high availability and performance during peak periods
requirements.assumptions: Traffic patterns are predictable and can be modeled
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System handles 50% increase in traffic without degradation in performance

criteria.reasoning: The system must comply with IRDAI regulations, implying that the requirements are well known and already documented in a 200-page RFP.
The requirement is for a claims processing portal for rural customers, implying that the full set of requirements can be pinned down before build starts.
The team has 15 developers and funding is approved for 18 months, implying that the requirements are stable and will not change once signed off.
The requirement is for a user-friendly interface, implying that stakeholders have a clear idea of what they want and do not need to see something working before they can say what they want.
The requirement is for the system to be scalable, implying that technical feasibility is not in doubt and a proof of concept is not required to demonstrate capability.
The requirements imply a new system for the organization, but do not indicate a new product direction.
The system must integrate with existing insurance company databases for claims processing.
The problem statement says the team has 15 developers and funding is approved for 18 months, implying a new system is being built, not an enhancement to an existing one.
UNSUPPORTED (claimed yes, nothing traceable to the problem statement): The problem statement says funding is approved for 18 months, implying stable funding throughout the life cycle.
The problem statement says the system must comply with IRDAI regulations, implying a long-lived infrastructure system.
The problem statement does not mention formal verification and testing at multiple stages, implying a traditional waterfall or V-model approach.
The statement does not mention the team's experience in the problem domain.
The statement does not mention the team's experience with the technology domain.
The statement does not mention the team's familiarity with the tools to be used on the project.

The statement does not mention training, upskilling, or onboarding being available for the project team.
The problem statement does not mention the availability of user representatives.

The problem statement does not mention the user representatives' expertise in the problem domain.

justifications.gives_up: Waterfall assumes the system stands on its own, and that the users do not want to be involved throughout — neither is true here, so that part of its design earns nothing on this project.

sdlc.summary: The project's predictable schedule, clear phase gates, and stable requirements make Waterfall the best choice. The project's need for user representatives and system integration also align with Waterfall's assumptions.
sdlc.shortcut: Predictable schedule + Clear phase gates + Stable requirements -> Waterfall
sdlc.cross_check_reasoning: Agile fits because it allows for flexibility and adaptability in response to changing requirements, such as the need for real-time updates to customers on claim status (REQ-004) and the integration with existing insurance company databases (REQ-002). Incremental fits because it allows for phased development and delivery of the system, which is suitable for a system with multiple high-priority requirements (REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003) and a need for scalability (REQ-005).
